title: Tourism service supply chains in ten emerging economies: data collection and analysis notebooks
description:
Notebooks documenting how a corpus of user-generated tourism reviews was retrieved from the Google Places API and how it was analysed, for a study of tourism service supply chains in ten emerging economies (51,037 reviews, 11,500 providers, 29 cities).

Contents. A collection notebook documenting the retrieval protocol, which runs in a dry-run mode issuing no API calls; and an analysis notebook implementing text normalisation, dictionary-based construct coding with negation handling, and logistic regressions with city fixed effects and supplier-clustered standard errors, together with the frozen coding dictionaries.

Data availability. No review data is distributed. Google Maps Platform policies permit indefinite storage of place identifiers only; review text, author names, ratings and related Places content may not be pre-fetched, cached or retained outside the permitted exceptions. The raw corpus is therefore neither redistributed nor available on request, and reviewer display names, which were processed only for deduplication, appear in no released file. What is deposited is the method: an independent researcher with their own API credentials can reconstruct an equivalent corpus from the documented protocol and re-run the analysis end to end. Re-execution does not reproduce the same corpus, since the platform returns a relevance-ranked subset that changes continuously.

Measurement status. The coding dictionaries have not been validated against independent human coding. A held-out double-coded validation protocol was prepared but had not been executed at this version. No precision, sensitivity or inter-coder agreement statistics are reported.
